evidence: The reviewer's claim that newIssueID produces 'lit-<workspacePrefix>-<8-char uuid>' matches the PR summary (store.go prefix change), so 'lit-124' examples misrepresent the ID shape. The thread has no reply but is outdated and the PR has a second commit; the packet does not show whether that commit applied the suggestion.
guidance_note: When renaming an identifier prefix, grep every example and fixture that hard-codes the old ID shape and replace it with a placeholder or a real-format example.

narrative: Mechanical lk-to-lit rename. One reviewer finding pointed out that the quickstart examples use a made-up ID format. The thread got no reply; it went outdated after a second commit, but the packet does not show whether that commit fixed it.
guidance_observations: Silent resolution with no reply leaves no record of whether a finding was fixed or dismissed.

evidence: The hunk's else-branch upserts the managed section into any existing pre-push hook with no interpreter check, so a python or /bin/sh hook gets shell lines it cannot run. The thread was resolved with no reply and is not outdated, so the code shipped unchanged.
guidance_note: Before splicing generated code into a user-owned file, enumerate the shapes that file can take (no shebang, sh, bash, python) and decide each one explicitly.

evidence: The claim depends on ExitCode()'s keyword mapping, which the packet does not show. If the mapping really is keyword-based, the sound fix is a typed ExitCode case for BeadsMigrationRequiredError, not rewording the message to hit a keyword.
guidance_note: When adding a new error type to a CLI with documented exit codes, map it explicitly in the exit-code classifier in the same change.

evidence: The hunk stops at 'if changed {' and does not show the fallback the reviewer says deletes the file when keep && !changed. If that fallthrough exists, it is a data-loss bug; the packet does not show it, and the thread was resolved with no reply.
guidance_note: For a destructive cleanup planner, write the (keep, changed) truth table first and give every cell an explicit return.

narrative: Large init/migrate PR, one review round with three findings. All three threads were resolved with no reply and none went outdated, so no visible change answered them. F1, a real hook-corruption risk for non-bash hooks, appears to have shipped as-is.
guidance_observations: Resolving threads with no reply or code change discards real findings without any recorded reasoning.

evidence: The runReady error used '[--columns ...]' while help used a different form, which is a real inconsistency. The agent aligned both on the short form and updated the test, 'to keep one canonical usage string', which resolves the drift just as well as the reviewer's direction.
guidance_note: Derive usage-error strings and help text from one constant so they cannot diverge.

narrative: Small feature PR with one usage-string inconsistency. The agent fixed it by aligning on the other form, which is equally valid.

evidence: hashExport marshals the whole export, including ExportedAt, which the reviewer says Export() sets to time.Now(), so the local and base hashes would almost never match. The agent dropped this code from the PR by reducing scope; the packet does not show whether the same hashExport landed through another PR with the bug intact.
guidance_note: When dropping code from a PR in response to a finding about it, carry the finding to wherever that code lands instead of letting it lapse.

evidence: The diff carried init/migrate, revision removal and the rename under a sync-pull title. The agent rewrote the PR to a single commit touching two files.
guidance_note: Branch from current master for each unit of work so unrelated in-flight changes do not ride along.

narrative: The PR was opened from a branch carrying much unrelated work. The reviewer flagged both the scope and a hash bug inside the unrelated code. The agent cut the PR down to its stated scope, which removed the hash bug from this PR without showing that it was fixed anywhere.
guidance_observations: Opening a PR from a stale or overloaded branch spends review effort on code that is about to be removed.

evidence: The claim that the config and DB live under git-common-dir, shared across worktrees, is not checkable from this README-only packet. The owner closed the PR as 'this work was not desired', so no response was ever needed.
The closeout block's 'lit sync push --remote origin --branch main' lacks --json while every other line in the block has it. The PR was closed as undesired, so the omission never shipped.

narrative: README rewrite the owner rejected ('this work was not desired') before any response. Neither finding matters to the outcome.
guidance_observations: The agent produced an unrequested README rewrite; confirm that doc reframing is wanted before opening the PR.

evidence: consumeOutputModeFlags scans all of argv and consumes any '--output'/'--json' token, so 'lit new --title --output' loses its value. The agent added a '--' sentinel and value-flag tracking, with regression tests.
guidance_note: When pre-scanning argv ahead of a real flag parser, list the token positions (flag value, after '--', positional) and handle each one.

evidence: The tests covered only ls and completion, and F5 shows that ready/init/migrate really were missing from the support list. The agent added coverage for those commands.
guidance_note: When a feature is gated by a hard-coded command list, test one command from each category the list is meant to cover.

evidence: The hunk shows '## Common commands' immediately followed by '## Output mode', which leaves the first section empty. The agent made it a subsection.
applyResolvedOutputMode strips only the exact token '--json', so '--json=false' survives and a trailing '--json' gets appended. The agent now handles the '--json=...' forms.
guidance_note: When normalizing a Go boolean flag, cover every form Go's flag package accepts ('-x', '--x', '--x=true', '--x=false').

evidence: commandSupportsOutputMode omits init, ready and migrate even though they support --json. The agent added them, and the F2 tests now catch future omissions, which covers most of the drift risk the reviewer's alternative (derive the list) addressed.
guidance_note: When introducing a whitelist of commands, generate it from the command registry or test it against the registry.

narrative: Output-mode normalization layer. One round, five accurate findings (argv pre-scan edge cases, a missing command list entry, a doc heading), all fixed in one commit with tests. No further rounds.
guidance_observations: Hand-rolled argv pre-scanning bought three edge-case findings; enumerating Go flag syntax forms up front would have covered them.

evidence: transitionIssueWithRetry calls time.Sleep(50ms) and ignores ctx. The agent switched to waitWithContext. Judging from the jitter constants a5a5e22 later modifies, the fix also moved the retry into the store and added exponential backoff with jitter.
guidance_note: Any sleep inside a ctx-carrying function must select on ctx.Done().

evidence: The reviewer itself concedes 'current callers only pass non-nil errors', so the nil guard is defensive code for an impossible input. Loosening the exact-phrase match to key substrings is a fair robustness point. The agent took both without separating them.
guidance_note: Split a bundled finding: accept the matching-robustness half, decline guards for inputs the call graph already rules out.

evidence: The new retry loop had no tests. The agent added tests for transient success, non-transient no-retry, cancel during backoff, and the classifier.
guidance_note: Ship retry logic with injected sleep/delay seams and tests in the same commit.

evidence: gofrs/flock's TryLockContext(ctx, retryDelay) retries every retryDelay until it acquires the lock or ctx is done; 50ms is the poll interval, not a timeout. The code's own '!locked' branch checks ctx.Err() first, consistent with that. The library semantics come from my knowledge of gofrs/flock, not from the packet. The agent accepted and built bounded polling plus stale-lock cleanup, the machinery PR #17 later had to repair. Flag false positive for caused_by: a5a5e22 added the commit lock as new work, not as a fix for any round-0 finding.
guidance_note: Before accepting a claim about a library call's timeout semantics, read the function's doc comment; here it says retryDelay is a poll interval.

evidence: The round-0 code used a fixed 50ms sleep. a5a5e22 edits pre-existing jitter/max-delay constants, so the F1 fix introduced exponential backoff with jitter and left the 'fixed backoff' description stale. With writers serialized by the commit lock, jitter adds little, so making the delay deterministic is a reasonable way to restore agreement.
guidance_note: When a fix changes a behavior the PR description names, update the description in the same push.

narrative: Retry PR whose round-0 fixes grew into a store-level retry plus a new cross-process commit lock. Round 1 flagged the lock's acquisition and the drift from 'fixed backoff' introduced by the F1 fix. The agent accepted F4's wrong premise about TryLockContext timing out and added polling and stale-lock cleanup, code that PR #17 then had to fix for stale-owner races.
guidance_observations: Adding new scope (a file lock) while addressing review findings made round 1 review an unrequested design.
Accepting a library-semantics claim without reading the library doc led to extra machinery and a follow-up P0 PR.

evidence: 'ADD COLUMN work_status ... NOT NULL DEFAULT 'todo'' backfills closed rows with 'todo', and both normalization UPDATEs touch only empty or invalid values. The agent added an explicit closed-implies-done backfill.
guidance_note: When adding a NOT NULL DEFAULT column derived from existing state, backfill from that state unconditionally rather than only fixing empty values.

evidence: The diff changed the created history entry's to_status from 'open' to issue.WorkStatus, mixing two state domains in one column. The agent restored 'open'.
guidance_note: Don't write values from a new state domain into columns named for the old one; give the new domain its own field.

evidence: The error said 'work_status' while users type 'work-status' or 'work:'. The agent reworded it.

start/done route through runTransition, whose flag descriptions say 'Lifecycle'. The agent made them generic. The packet does not show whether those descriptions ever render, given SetOutput(io.Discard).

narrative: work_status feature with four accurate findings, all fixed. The owner then closed the PR to redo it to match beads (resubmitted as PR #14).
guidance_observations: Check compatibility with the reference system (beads) before designing a new state field.

evidence: The packet does not show the Run routing, and isCommandHelpRequest might intercept 'help --help' before runHelp sees ['--help']. The PR was superseded by #11 without a response.

PR #11's diff shows the same '[LAW:one-source-of-truth] Command help metadata is centralized...' comment next to a hard-coded printUsage listing every command again. The finding was not carried into #11, where the reviewer raised it again as #11/F2.
guidance_note: Don't attach a single-source-of-truth claim to a catalog unless every renderer reads from it.

evidence: isCommandHelpRequest scans all of args[1:] with no '--' stop, so '--reason -h' triggers help. The PR was superseded by #11; the packet does not show whether #11 kept this scan (argsContainHelp appears there).
guidance_note: A help-flag scan must stop at '--' and skip flag values, the same rule as any argv pre-scan (see #6/F1).

narrative: Help UX PR superseded by #11 without answering its three findings. Two of them (help --help, the single-source-of-truth comment) were raised again on #11, so the reviewer paid for them twice.
guidance_observations: When superseding a PR, carry its open findings into the successor instead of letting the reviewer rediscover them.

evidence: The custom help command with DisableFlagParsing passes '--help' to runHelp as a positional arg. 10a4d94 deleted the custom help command and runHelp and fell back to Cobra's native help, which removes the bug. There was no reply on the thread.

The 10a4d94 diff shows printUsage hard-coding the full command list next to commandHelpCatalog. The commit deleted both and used Cobra groups, which resolves the duplication; but dropping the catalog's Usage lines caused F3. There was no reply on the thread.
guidance_note: When deleting a duplicated data source, check what information only that source carried (here, per-command flag syntax) and move it somewhere before deleting.

evidence: Before 10a4d94, 'lit <cmd> --help' printed the catalog entry's Usage line with the flags. After it, cmd.Help() shows only the generic agentCommandHelp Long text, because the wrappers declare no Cobra flags. The thread was resolved with no reply and is not outdated.
guidance_note: When replacing a help renderer, compare 'lit new --help' output before and after the swap.

evidence: runWithWorkspace calls enforceBeadsPreflight and then resolveWorkspaceFromWD. The packet does not show enforceBeadsPreflight's body, though the removed pre-PR code did call workspace.Resolve inside preflight. Flag false positive for caused_by: 10a4d94 only re-wrapped call sites, and runWithWorkspace's body is unchanged from round 0.
guidance_note: When extracting a preflight helper, return what it resolved so callers don't repeat the lookup.

narrative: Cobra migration. Round 0 raised the same help bugs as #10; the agent fixed them silently in 10a4d94 by deleting the custom help catalog. That deletion threw away the per-command flag syntax, so round 1 flagged that '--help' no longer shows flags. That thread was resolved with no reply and appears unfixed at merge.
guidance_observations: Fixes pushed with no thread replies leave no record of which finding each change answered.
The PR merged with a resolved-but-unanswered regression finding (F3).

evidence: The file states a deliberate operating policy ('No encountered changes are considered unexpected enough to interrupt workflow'). The reviewer wants to add escalation carve-outs the policy's author intentionally excluded, which is a preference against the owner's directive, not a defect. The PR was closed unmerged.
The risk of the doc diverging from AGENTS.md is real, but the suggested sentence invents a scope split ('shared policies' vs 'workflow-specific') that nobody specified. The PR was closed unmerged.
'valuable' is subjective, but the suggested definitions narrow 'incidental' to formatting or mechanical edits, which changes the policy rather than clarifying it. The PR was closed unmerged.

The bullets do repeat 'don't interrupt'. For agent-directed policy, repetition is often deliberate emphasis, and the suggested consolidation keeps all four restatements as sub-bullets anyway. The PR was closed unmerged.

narrative: Ten-line agent-policy doc. The reviewer's four findings mostly try to soften or redefine an owner directive. The PR was closed unmerged with no replies, so none of it mattered.
guidance_observations: Reviewer findings on owner-authored policy text are usually preference, not defect, and warrant pushback rather than edits.

evidence: The hunk calls 'branch --show-current' unconditionally and returns its error, so a plain push with no --branch could fail on a lookup it does not need. The agent made the lookup conditional on --branch, the reviewer's first option rather than the silent fallback, and added tests.
guidance_note: Do an extra subprocess call only on the path whose output depends on it.

narrative: Small push-refspec fix. The one finding was accurate, and the agent chose the cleaner of the two options the reviewer offered.

evidence: The UPDATE writes closed_at = NULL for non-closed transitions, but the returned struct only sets ClosedAt when closing, so the in-memory value can disagree with the row. The migration's 'UPDATE issues SET closed_at = NULL WHERE status <> closed' makes a stale value unlikely, hence partly. The PR merged two minutes before the review posted.
guidance_note: Return the entity re-read from the row you wrote, or set every column the UPDATE set, so the return value cannot drift from the database.

evidence: normalizeStatus maps '' to 'open', so an import missing status is silently rewritten instead of rejected, which the reviewer says reverses the prior ImportIssue validation. It went unanswered because the PR merged before the review.
guidance_note: Keep strict parsing and defaulting as separate functions, with defaults only at the call site that wants them (CreateIssue), never on the import path.

evidence: ensureStatusConstraint drops old CHECKs and adds a new one, but the reviewer notes the tests cover only the work_status drop path. Upgrading from the legacy CHECK(status IN ('open','closed')) is the path existing installs take, and it is untested.
guidance_note: A schema migration needs a test that seeds the previous production schema and runs Open().

evidence: normalizeQueryStatus repeats store.normalizeStatus's trim/lower, 'in-progress' alias and allowed set almost line for line. The only difference is how '' is treated, which is itself the F2 inconsistency.
guidance_note: When adding a canonical enum, export one parser and one constant set from the owning package and import them in every consumer.

narrative: Redo of #9 using a single status field. It merged two minutes before Copilot's review landed, so four accurate findings (silent status default on import, duplicated normalizer, untested legacy-constraint migration, a stale ClosedAt in the return value) went unanswered.
guidance_observations: Merging before the requested review finishes shipped every finding it raised.

evidence: validateNestedCommandPath checks containsHelpFlag(args) over all args, so 'lit dep add --help' gets the dep-level usage error. The agent restricted the check to args[0] and added a pass-through test.
guidance_note: When adding a help-flag scan, test help at every nesting level ('lit dep --help' and 'lit dep add --help').

narrative: Fix for nested-command startup side effects and the runWithApp context deadlock. One accurate finding about help-flag scope, fixed with a test. This is the third PR in the batch where a whole-argv flag scan caused a finding (#6/F1, #10/F3).
guidance_observations: The same argv-scan mistake recurred across three PRs; a shared, tested argv helper would close the whole class.

evidence: readCommandLockOwnerPID returns hasOwnerPID=false for empty content and the caller returns stale=true, so a lock file caught between creation and the PID write can be deleted out from under a live holder. That race is worse than the I/O-error case the reviewer named. The thread was resolved with no reply and is not outdated.
guidance_note: Never treat 'no readable owner' as 'dead owner'; require age-staleness too, or write the PID atomically before the lock becomes visible.

evidence: The same empty-means-stale logic is duplicated in readCommitLockOwnerPID/commitLockOwnedByDeadProcess, with the same create-then-write race. The thread was resolved with no reply and is not outdated.
guidance_note: Two copies of the lock-owner probe in cli and store should be one helper, so a fix lands once.

evidence: Liveness is decided by substring-matching err.Error(), whereas Process.Signal on Unix returns syscall.Errno, which errors.Is(err, syscall.ESRCH) checks stably. The thread is outdated after a second commit, but the packet does not show what changed.
guidance_note: Classify OS errors by errno (errors.Is with syscall constants), never by message text.

evidence: isCommandLockPIDRunning is a byte-for-byte copy of the commit-lock probe with the same string matching. The thread is outdated, but the packet does not show the follow-up change.
guidance_note: Write the PID-liveness probe once and share it, instead of copying it into cli and store.

evidence: The goroutine leak on timeout is real, but a deadlocked Run may not honor ctx cancellation, so the suggested context.WithTimeout only helps if the deadlock path selects on ctx. The thread is outdated, but the packet does not show the change.

narrative: P0 deadlock and stale-lock recovery fix, merged six minutes after review with no thread replies. The stale-lock cleanup traces back to #8, where the agent accepted a wrong premise about TryLockContext and added stale-lock removal. Here, empty PID content is treated as a dead owner, which opens a create-then-write race that went unaddressed (F1/F2, not outdated). The PID-liveness probe is duplicated across cli and store.
guidance_observations: Merging minutes after review with zero replies shipped a lock-safety race on a P0 fix.
Duplicating the lock-owner probe in two packages doubled every finding.
